channel.title: Social Media Today - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Social Media Today (socialmediatoday.com)

item.title: Film studio association issues new censure against ByteDance’s AI tool
item.description: The Motion Picture Association sent a strongly worded letter to the Seedance owner demanding that it stop training on copyrighted material, per Variety.

item.title: Instagram emphasizes Reels in new design update
item.description: Customizable feed options and a new Your Feeds center give users another way to access Reels content, according to an app researcher.

item.title: X tests AI labeling to combat the rise of generated content
item.description: The app is working on a process that would require users to label posts created using artificial intelligence tools, according to an app researcher.

item.title: Professional AI adoption could unlock up to $4.1 trillion capacity for US
item.description: A new report from LinkedIn found that more needs to be done in order to maximize the benefit of artificial intelligence in the workforce.

item.title: Pinterest publishes inaugural Parenting Trend Report
item.description: The research highlighted seven key trends and showcased how parents are using Pins to plan vacations and create at-home activities.

item.title: TikTok expands its MLB partnership agreement
item.description: The multi-year deal builds on an existing agreement with the league and will offer exclusive in-app content, including highlights and insights.

item.title: Meta signs long-term supply deal with AMD for AI hardware
item.description: The partnership builds on the companies’ existing collaboration and will help expand Meta’s compute power.

item.title: U.S. Department of War signs deal with xAI
item.description: The partnership will allow defense applications and military systems to work with Grok’s models, per an Axios report.

item.title: LinkedIn ID verification partner Persona under fire for security concerns
item.description: A researcher from The Local Stack reported potential data collection questions, leading companies including Discord to re-evaluate the system.

item.title: LinkedIn shares top skills on the rise in marketing for 2026
item.description: Social media branding, community engagement and performance analysis were all key trends highlighted in the platform’s annual list.
